timeline.label: Kojiki completed
timeline.caption: A court compilation of myth, genealogy, and remembered tradition.

timeline.label: Nihon Shoki completed
timeline.caption: The court's chronicle framed the prehistoric past from an eighth-century political world.

genealogy.caption: This is a retrospective court genealogy, not a contemporary record of prehistoric succession.

timeline.label: Earliest secure occupation
timeline.caption: Secure evidence appears in the main islands and Ryukyu chain during this broad interval.

timeline.label: Paleolithic hoax exposed
timeline.caption: Exposure of planted artifacts forced reassessment of claims for much earlier occupation.

timeline.label: Aira eruption
timeline.caption: The eruption left a widespread ash marker and transformed southern environments.

timeline.label: Late Paleolithic
timeline.caption: Regional stone industries and mobile lifeways developed across the archipelago.

timeline.label: Odai Yamamoto I pottery
timeline.caption: Calibrated residue dates place pottery production in the closing Pleistocene.

timeline.label: Incipient Jomon
timeline.caption: Pottery and new subsistence practices spread unevenly before the Holocene.

timeline.label: Jomon sequence
timeline.display_date: ca. 14,500 BC–regional first millennium BC endings
timeline.caption: Dates and period boundaries differ by region.

timeline.label: Sannai Maruyama occupation
timeline.caption: Repeated construction formed a durable settlement and gathering place in northern Honshu.

timeline.label: Early to Middle Jomon growth
timeline.caption: Many regions show denser settlement and intensified woodland and aquatic resource use.

timeline.label: Long-distance Jomon exchange
timeline.caption: Obsidian, jade, asphalt, amber, and shell moved through overlapping regional networks.

timeline.label: Dogu traditions
timeline.caption: Clay figurines varied substantially across time and place.

timeline.label: Late and Final Jomon reorganization
timeline.caption: Settlement contraction and new ritual and exchange patterns unfolded unevenly.

timeline.label: Wet-rice farming in northern Kyushu
timeline.caption: AMS dating places early paddy agriculture centuries earlier than the older conventional chronology.

timeline.label: Agricultural dispersal
timeline.caption: Farming spread east at different rates while mixed economies continued.

timeline.label: Yayoi period
timeline.display_date: ca. tenth century BC–third century AD, regionally
timeline.caption: Agricultural villages, hierarchy, exchange, and conflict developed unevenly.

timeline.label: Yoshinogari growth
timeline.display_date: ca. fourth century BC–third century AD
timeline.caption: Successive phases created a major enclosed center in northern Kyushu.

timeline.label: Bronze ritual traditions
timeline.display_date: ca. fourth century BC–second century AD
timeline.caption: Weapon-shaped bronzes, dotaku bells, and mirrors marked changing ritual and political networks.

timeline.label: Yayoi migration and admixture
timeline.caption: Population movement and mixture continued at different rates and extended into the Kofun age.

timeline.label: Na embassy to Later Han
timeline.caption: The Later Han history records an embassy and an imperial seal.

timeline.label: Wa embassy
timeline.caption: A second recorded embassy reached the Later Han court.

timeline.label: Wei account of Wa
timeline.caption: The dynastic history describes many Wa polities and the federation of Yamatai.

timeline.label: Himiko's embassy to Wei
timeline.caption: Yamatai entered a formal diplomatic relationship with the Wei court.

timeline.label: Death of Himiko
timeline.caption: The account reports burial, disorder, and a later female succession.

timeline.label: Earliest keyhole-mound horizon
timeline.caption: Large standardized mounds signal the political transformation developed in the next chapter.

genealogy.caption: The links reproduce only the succession and kinship stated by the Wei account.
